video_title: Boogie - Cavs QUIT After Game 1! + Should Cavs FIRE Atkinson?

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on Cavaliers' lack of fight after Game 1
quotes.excerpt: It just didn't seem like a group that really, really wanted it.
quotes.quote: I would say I didn't see much of a fight or an effort outside of that, you know, that 20-plus point lead Game 1. After that, it seemed like it was a team that wasn't really interested in competing or, you know, trying to advance to a Finals. And I'm, you know, I'm on the outside looking in, but, you know, the force, the fight wasn't really there throughout the rest of the series. It kind of looked like it was it kind of looked like fluff until, you know, towards the end and they could just kind of, you know, the term I like to use is tuck your tail. It seemed like they tucked their tail after the, you know, the first half usually, but it just didn't seem like a group that really, really wanted it. There's a lot of things you can kind of dissect as far as what you think wrong with went wrong with Cleveland, but I'll keep it pretty short and brief. It just didn't seem like a group that that that was there to advance.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on Cavaliers' loss of toughness and competitive spirit
quotes.excerpt: I didn't see a lot of competitive fight last night.
quotes.quote: I think they lost something with no Schroder. Once you once you see no Schroder in a game like that that's not going to give you physicality, not going to give you that toughness that they needed, I felt like they lost a lot right there and and one of their best role players. Other than that, nobody else competed. I'll say it. I think last night, they had to make a decision what they wanted to get back on that plane or not and do this again. And I think they made the decision, we cool. We outgunned and outmanned and we going to stay right here in our building and we going to lose it like this. I didn't see a lot of competitive fight last night. Like last night you let a team go out and get almost 40 points in the first quarter. That should tell you everything you need to know about where they were competitively and them trying to give themselves another opportunity to compete in this series. I didn't see it last night.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on Cavaliers' early mental defeat and quitting
quotes.excerpt: They can just tuck their tail and pack it in early.
quotes.quote: You know what this reminded me of guys? Like, you know that last game before All-Star Weekend when like you just you kind of start thinking what plans we got, when is the flight, when or where are we going? I feel like once they got kicked in the mouth early last night and they went down double digits, it was a wrap. And I was all over the Knicks last night because of that exact reason. Like, are we really going to get on a plane and go back to New York just to lose in five? Like, and it just feels like they were just defeated right off the rip and they never had a chance. And there was a level of them quitting because they just knew this series was over and this game was over and and they're just going to pack it in and, hey, we made it to the Conference Finals. We'll we'll we still got our young guys, our core under contract, we still have a lot of talent, still have a good coach. I think that starts playing into when you get down the way they got down. I mean, they got their ass kicked and this was over this was over before it even begun really. So I think there was a moment in time where like they like they like Boogie said, they can just tuck their tail and pack it in early and the Knicks did a great job making that a point to get off to an early start to to allow them to do that.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Michelle Beadle on Cavaliers' lack of mental strength
quotes.excerpt: They just never showed that they were that team that would be able to do that as far as like mental strength was concerned.
quotes.quote: I just think this Cleveland team never showed that, you know, yeah, we've seen teams get down 22, even lose games after being up by that much. They just never showed that they were that team that would be able to do that as far as like mental strength was concerned, which is exactly how this played out. They did go down 3-0.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Atkinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson on Cavaliers' analytics despite the sweep
quotes.excerpt: Analytically, I think we won the expect I said three out of three, we're two out of three in the expected.
quotes.quote: Analytically, I think we won the expect I said three out of three, we're two out of three in the expected, if you guys follow that, there's an expected score. You know, and we won two out of three. I know you're looking confused, but I there there is really, you know, if you believe in process and all that, like, man, our so you know, take that later.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Panel reacts to Kenny Atkinson's confusing analytics comment
quotes.excerpt: What in the hell does that even mean?

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: What in the hell does that even mean? Anybody? Who who wants to take the analytics route on this bad boy? Boogie looks like he's ready.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: And listen, I but I I've been consistent in how I feel about basketball. You got numbers guys, and you got vibe guys. I'm a vibe guy. I'm a vibe check guy.

text_blocks.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
text_blocks.text: I know it.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams criticizes Kenny Atkinson's analytics-focused message after sweep
quotes.excerpt: At some point, you got to throw that in the trash can and you just got to compete and play basketball.
quotes.quote: I got to go out there and look you in your eyes and say, are you willing to compete? I don't care about numbers. I don't care about what the numbers say works best for us. At some point, you got to throw that in the trash can and you just got to compete and play basketball. So on paper, whatever analytical numbers they were looking for to say that they won a game, it didn't win a game. It didn't win a game, coach. So I don't I don't want to hear this if I'm a fan. I don't want to hear this if I'm the front office, and I damn sure don't want to hear it if I'm in uniform. Is that a a a nice way of trying to ease over the pain of being down 0-3 at that time? Whatever the message was that he was trying to get across, optically this just sounded bad, it looked bad. And it just and it and it sets the standard for your for your team. And I and I've said it publicly, man, I love Kenny Atkinson to death. This is one of my favorite people that I've ever worked with in the business. He's responsible for getting me back on my feet in my career after I tore my ACL. We worked side by side every day of the week. But this messaging is just bad, man. I got to call a spade a spade. The messaging was bad. So, you know, you allow a lot of analytical guys into the game and think that's the way that's the way to win a championship, then this proved that it's not. It's a it's a great asset to have to combine it with the things that you need to do physically on the floor to win a basketball game, but it shouldn't be your end all be all. I didn't love this message.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons argues analytics are meaningless without effort
quotes.excerpt: That means nothing when you get outworked and outplayed and out-rebounded and turn the ball over way more.
quotes.quote: It's almost like saying the sweep wasn't as bad as it looked. Like because analytically we were right in it. Like I think that's maybe the but that's like Lou just said, that means nothing when you get outworked and outplayed and out-rebounded and turn the ball over way more and give up 50 points in transition. Like analytically, that means nothing. So I just think again like Lou just said, optics, it's just a soft message to me. It's like, well, analytically we hung in there even though we got punked for 48 minutes for four straight games. It means nothing.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams and Chandler Parsons question the value of analytics
quotes.excerpt: I want to see those analytical stats.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: I want to see those analytical stats. Like, give me those stats.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Optics, like, it's just a soft message to me. It's like, well, analytically we hung in there even though we got punked for 48 minutes for four straight games. It means nothing.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on Cavaliers' season being a success despite sour ending
quotes.excerpt: To say it's a failure, I think is a stretch.
quotes.quote: This guy also said that James Harden's one of their best perimeter defenders, which is like, I don't know how you can watch the film. I don't even care analytically what it says. Like that Jalen Brunson end of game there in Game 1, like he you just can't you can't say that kind of stuff when it's just when it's not true. Like and so I get it. Analytically, I get it. It's just it's the one thing I do agree with what he said. He said the season was not a failure. It ended sour at the end of the day. And at the end of the day, they did make a trade. They did go to the Eastern Conference Finals. They did get further than they ever had with this group. To say it's a failure, I think is a stretch. The way it ended sucks. It's like the Pistons season. Like they didn't they like that that was a shitty ending to a great season. The Cavaliers, I think, can can hold their head high at least getting to the Eastern Conference Finals and having their core come back. And hopefully run it back. But it feels like we're saying this every single year about this team. Like they always leave us wanting more.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams argues Cavaliers' playoff round was a failure
quotes.excerpt: To fall short and can't even go get one game, that is considered a failure.
quotes.quote: Analytically, they had a better year this year than they did last year. Analytically. They got to another step. And I I'll I'll back you on that because if I go to the Eastern Conference Finals, you can't tell me my season you can't tell me my season was a was a failure. Your postseason, that this round was a failure. For you guys to go out, make the trade, put the group together to get to the point of competition that you built that team for and to fall short and can't even go get one game, that is considered a failure.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams warns other teams won't wait for Cavaliers' slow build
quotes.excerpt: Nobody is going to wait around for you guys to continue to slowly build step after step, block after block.
quotes.quote: Now, when you put everything into perspective to to trade away Garland, to bring in James Harden, to go out and get Keon Ellis and Schroder. Ellis made an impact early on. Schroder made an impact throughout with his presence. Those were positive steps. But at what point do you look in the mirror and say, you know what, we put this team together to win a championship and we didn't get there. So we got to consider that a failure. We got to consider that part of it a failure because you just mentioned earlier in the show, Chandler, the Celtics are going to get better. New York Knicks are where they are. Detroit is going to come back with a vengeance. Nobody is going to wait around for you guys to continue to slowly build step after step, block after block. Some of these teams are going to skip steps and they're going to get there. Atlanta Hawks, they'll be active this year and trying to make that team better. So everything around them is trending for them to go backwards if this is going to be your response to getting swept in the Eastern Conference Finals. So is it a complete failure? No, but you got to take some accountability and say, we didn't reach the level that we wanted to reach with this group.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins argues Cavaliers' season was a success, not a failure
quotes.excerpt: Analytics can't determine fight. Analytics can't determine heart. Analytics can't determine leadership.
quotes.quote: I don't think it's a failure at all. I think they I think they achieved more than they did the previous season. So when you look at it in that way, obviously that's progress. That's progress. We all can agree on that part. But as far as the analytics, that's my that's my whole issue with it. Analytics can't determine fight. Analytics can't determine heart. Analytics can't determine leadership. And that's all three things that this Cleveland team was missing in this series. So to throw out, you know, all these analytical stats is it's kind of it's kind of smoke and mirrors. It's it's pointless.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins defends Cavaliers' season as a success
quotes.excerpt: To make a splash like that mid-season and then end your season with a Conference Finals loss, I wouldn't necessarily say that's a failure.
quotes.quote: I don't agree with that part. I think it's absolute bullshit to be honest. But as far as their overall season, I would say it was a success. They made a big splash when they decided to trade for James Harden and trade away a young asset in and Garland. And it was a first-time All-Star as well if I believe. But, you know, to make a splash like that mid-season and then end your season with a Conference Conference Finals loss, I wouldn't necessarily say that's a failure. So in that, looking at it through that lens, they had a successful season.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Panel debates if Cavaliers' sweep warrants coaching changes or is a building block
quotes.excerpt: If there's no heart and leadership in that locker room, these dudes have been there with the exception of James Harden and nothing's changing.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: So I'm a little confused, right? And I'm going to get to James Harden in a second. But we just talked about lack of heart, lack of leadership, lack of this, that and the other. Talking about putting lipstick on a pig when you try to point out analytics and somehow make it seem like not as bad. If all that is true and obviously it was, because you just got swept, not close, like you got swept, swept, then this can't be considered something to build on moving forward at all. Because nothing that you just named is fundamentally sound in moving forward. If there's no heart and leadership in that locker room, these dudes have been there with the exception of James Harden and nothing's changing. Like you're just taking these incremental tiny steps. I feel like a lot of things should change. I don't think Kenny Atkinson keeps his job.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: But that's a big step.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: Is it a big step? Because they're not going to change personality by next season. They are who they are.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: No, but there's a couple of big pieces that can change everything about this group that are probably sort itself out. James Harden, free agent.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on James Harden's future and Kenny Atkinson's job security
quotes.excerpt: I don't know if it's just a shoe-in to fire Kenny Atkinson.
quotes.quote: That's a big piece right there. So do you keep him? Do you not keep him then? Because you're going to want money. I think you take a I think you take a serious you take a serious look at it. Like, you know, there's not a lot of James Hardens walking around on the streets. Now, granted, he didn't play he didn't play great basketball. He's at the end of his career. He's a he's an older guy. But you also have to consider the namesake. It's James Harden. So, but if you're the Cleveland Cavaliers, you're weighing all of your options. I don't know if it's just a shoe-in to fire Kenny Atkinson. We're talking about a a guy that was the coach of the year two seasons removed. I think he's a quality coach, but I think he got out-coached this round.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Panel debates whether a playoff sweep warrants firing the coach
quotes.excerpt: I'm not a fan of just losing your job every time something goes wrong in this world of sports.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: I think he's a quality coach, but I think he got out-coached this round. So does it necessarily mean he's a bad coach? Does that necessarily mean that you don't go find another Kenny Atkinson out there with with some of these coaches available? Who knows? That's going to be a lot of conversations. So just because something goes wrong, I'm not a I'm not a fan of just losing your job every time something goes wrong in this in this world of of sports. There has to be a yeah, it has to it has to be some consistency in that. But if it's not if it's not what you're looking for, then you look at that if you're Dan Gilbert. But I but just because you get swept and it looks bad, you still got to the Eastern Conference Finals. There were some positive things that happened. You just don't lose your jobs because of that.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Stop, stop saying that.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: That was a hard sweep. That was a hard sweep. That wasn't just like, oh, we were in it. We went to overtime.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: But but again, it's it's not your reality. It's not your reality, but.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Panel debates if playoff expectations justify firing a coach
quotes.excerpt: Everybody's expectation is to win a championship, Beadle.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: You got humiliated. I think he loses his job and I think that's right.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: If San Antonio is down is down two games right now, we're not asking for Miss Johnson's job. It's a process of these things.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: But it's different expectations. You went from winning last year.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: Everybody's expectation is to win a championship, Beadle.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: Cleveland already had last year as as a as what we consider a quote-unquote failure simply because they started the way they did and they absolutely fizzled out in the playoffs. You kept your job. Right? And they did better than that.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Panel debates owner's right to fire a coach vs. need for patience
quotes.excerpt: Owners, they are billionaires for reasons. They sort of go off a whim.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: As an owner, I'm not telling you like this is what I think I would do, but I'm telling you owners, they are billionaires for reasons. They sort of go off a whim and if they wake up this morning and decide, you know what, enough is enough, we got embarrassed, I'm just going to make a change. It doesn't have to make sense to us. And we've seen so many coaches of the year get booted within the next 700 days. So it's it is what it is.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: I can get that part, but we speaking like we supposed to respect him waking up and being emotional. Like, no, I don't I don't respect that. Now, can he do it in his that is right? Sure. But I'm just saying, I don't think that's the I don't think that's the best move. Again, did anybody expect them to be swept? No. Did they play bad? Yes. Was it embarrassing? Yes. But once everything settles down, you got to take a look at what you got inside of your locker room and who do you have coaching this basketball team and ask yourself, can I go out and get somebody that's going to get me over that hump? If the answer to that is no, and I feel pretty comfortable where I am, but I have to make some decisions to move forward, then you keep the core what you got going on. That's my opinion.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Yeah, like think about it. The league is really, really good, man. Like they they went to the Conference Finals. You know how many good teams there were this season?

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons advocates patience for Cavaliers' talented core
quotes.excerpt: They are going to be loaded again and they're going to be one of the more talented teams.
quotes.quote: And yes, it it ended embarrassingly and it ended in a really, really bad sweep to a team that's playing really, really good basketball. So yes, it sucks this morning. Yes, you have that sour taste in your mouth, but at the end of the day, Kenny Atkinson has got this team playing at a high level. We are talking about the Cavs no matter what happens with James Harden or whatever this summer. We are going to be talking about the Cavs as a home court advantage team next year with Donovan Mitchell, Jarrett Allen, Evan Mobley. And I think they're going to have to bring back James Harden because there's no way I'm trading Darius Garland for a half rental season of James Harden. Like he will be back in a Cavs jersey next year, which means they are going to be loaded again and they're going to be one of the more talented teams. So again, I do think NBA owners are short-sided. They want immediate results. They want championships and that's not really realistic. Let's be honest. Did we really have expectations for the Cavs to win a championship this year?
